(a) Authorization of Appropriations.—
        (1) In general.—Section 48103(7) of title 49, United States Code, is amended to read as follows:
“(7) $3,024,657,534 for the period beginning on October 1, 2009, and ending on July 3, 2010.”. 
        (2) Availability of amounts.—Sums made available pursuant to the amendment made by paragraph (1) shall remain available until expended. 
        (3) Program implementation.—For purposes of calculating funding apportionments and meeting other requirements under sections 47114, 47115, 47116, and 47117 of title 49, United States Code, for the period beginning on October 1, 2009, and ending on July 3, 2010, the Administrator of the Federal Aviation Administration shall—
            (A) first calculate funding apportionments on an annualized basis as if the total amount available under section 48103 of such title for fiscal year 2010 were $4,000,000,000; and 
            (B) then reduce by 17 percent—
                (i) all funding apportionments calculated under subparagraph (A); and 
                (ii) amounts available pursuant to sections 47117(b) and 47117(f)(2) of such title.    
    (b) Project Grant Authority.—Section 47104(c) of such title is amended by striking “April 30, 2010,” and inserting “July 3, 2010,”.

fable.w: This section only extends an authorization of appropriations and directs the FAA Administrator on how to calculate funding apportionments, then extends a project grant authority date. The tempting reading is that apportionments and grant authority involve airports and other outside recipients, but grant funding is not participation, and no outside party is consulted, heard, or given a right to sue. The only actor is a federal official doing internal funding calculations.
fable.s: the Administrator of the Federal Aviation Administration shall

opus.w: This section sets appropriation amounts, keeps the funds available until spent, tells the FAA Administrator how to calculate and cut funding apportionments, and extends the project grant authority date. It has no comment period, rulemaking, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outside parties, or right to sue. Grant apportionments and grant authority are benefit distribution, not participation, so the grant language does not make this a 'Yes'.
opus.b: The tempting reading is that "Project Grant Authority" and the funding apportionments to airports bring outside parties into a federal decision. That fails because the section only sets appropriation amounts, fixes how the FAA Administrator calculates apportionments, and extends a grant-authority deadline. No outside party is consulted, and grant distribution is excluded from the definition in any case.

qwen_chat.w: This section amends the deadline for project grant authority and adjusts funding calculations. It does not require consultation with outside parties, public hearings, or advisory committees. The definition explicitly excludes applications for grants from the scope of participation. All actors involved (FAA Administrator, Congress) are inside the federal government.
qwen_chat.s: (b) Project Grant Authority.—Section 47104(c) of such title is amended by striking “April 30, 2010,” and inserting “July 3, 2010,”.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that "Project Grant Authority" implies a process where outside parties apply for grants, and thus participate. However, the definition explicitly states: "It does not include applications for benefits or grants." Furthermore, the text only amends a date deadline for the authority to make grants; it does not describe a consultation, hearing, or advisory process involving outside parties in the decision-making itself. The actors mentioned (Administrator of FAA, Congress via appropriations) are all inside the federal government.
